subject: GPU headroom matrix for Skyline Health pilot — temporary autoscale allowance
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, pilot@skylinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GPU headroom matrix for Skyline Health pilot — temporary autoscale allowance

Team,

Skyline Health is aiming to run a 4-week pilot (starting Sept 6) that exercises our real-time summarization endpoint. They’ve given an early traffic profile and expect a sustained 75 qps with several 30–90s spikes up to ~180 qps during simulated peak clinical sessions. They asked whether we can provide a small dedicated pool and a short-lived autoscale override so they won’t be blocked by our default burst gating.

I did a first pass at a headroom matrix (attached) that maps requested vGPU slots by hour-of-day and a conservative burst cushion. Ask: can Product/Ops approve a temporary autoscale allowance for this pilot window and reserve a 12-slot dedicated pool in us-west for the duration? If we can’t allow autoscale overrides, we need a clear alternative (e.g., larger fixed pool or explicit scheduled bursts).

What I need from Ops/Product:
- Quick read on whether a temporary autoscale policy exemption is feasible for a 4-week pilot and what constraints we should attach (max burst, throttling, fallback).
- Confirmation on whether a 12-slot dedicated pool in us-west is feasible for Sept 6–Oct 4.
- Any runbook/guardrail language you want Sales to send to Skyline for the pilot (SLOs, cost exposure, telemetry hooks).

Attachments: headroom_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix by hour + projected cost delta) and pilot_runbook_draft.pdf (initial runbook).

Timeline: Skyline needs a clear answer by EOD Thu Aug 27 to finalize their internal approvals.

Thanks —
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU headroom matrix for Skyline Health pilot — temporary autoscale allowance

On Tue, Aug 25, 2026 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team,
> Skyline Health is aiming to run a 4-week pilot ...

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachments — the matrix is helpful. A few operational notes and constraints from Dedicated Capacity: 

1) Temporary autoscale overrides are operationally possible but we treat them as exceptions. We’d need: a signed acknowledgement of cost/risk from Sales, a max-burst cap (I’d propose 2x baseline, up to 24 slots total), and a monitoring hook with automatic rollback if error rate or GPU memory pressure exceeds thresholds.

2) 12-slot dedicated pool in us-west: technically feasible given current pool utilization for the requested window, but we need a soft hold placed today to avoid oversubscription. If you want that formalized I can open a reservation ticket (will hold for 48 hours pending exec signoff).

3) Please add an SRE on the thread for on-call coordination (I’ve cc’d Laura but will also request Ajay from SRE once we have the band agreed).

Action items for us:
- Kimberly to draft exact guardrail sentences for runbook (max-burst, rollback triggers, telemetry endpoints).
- Marcus to confirm commercial coverage and whether Skyline will sign a one-time charge or we convert to a trial credit.
- Neha to confirm pilot start/end and any security requirements that would change the deployment modality.

I’ll prepare a short ops playbook snippet and send it back with suggested thresholds by EOD Wed.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Capacity Operations
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, pilot@skylinehealth.com, accounts@skylinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GPU headroom matrix for Skyline Health pilot — temporary autoscale allowance

Neha / Kim —

From a commercial perspective we can cover the extra capacity for the pilot as follows: a) Skyline will sign a limited pilot MOU that accepts pass-through billing for peak usage, or b) Redwood can apply a capped pilot credit against expected overage; we prefer (a) because it keeps cost signals clear. I’ve tentatively allocated a $6k pilot buffer in the CRM deal (SKY-PI-2026-08) to cover small bursts; beyond that we’ll need a separate PO.

If Ops requires an explicit signed acknowledgement of risk/rollback, Sales can get that included in the MOU this week. Marcus will also coordinate with Finance for a one-time billing path if they want to do fixed-price.

One ask from Sales: please include the specific rollback thresholds and the monitoring endpoints in the runbook so our AE can explain them to Skyline’s ops lead.

I’ll also loop in GPU vendor sales (sales@gpucloud.io) for capacity validation at their end — they sometimes need prior notice for hot-swap provisioning.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Thanks, all — good alignment. Summary and next steps: 

1) Ops: Kimberly will open a soft hold for a 12-slot pool in us-west today and will circulate a short ops playbook (includes rollback triggers, telemetry endpoints, and max-burst = 24 slots).
2) Sales/Finance: Marcus will confirm whether Skyline signs the pilot MOU (preferred) or we apply the pilot buffer credit (backup). I’ve put the deal id in the ticket (SKY-PI-2026-08).
3) Runbook: I updated the attached pilot_runbook_draft.pdf with Kim’s requested fields (see attached v2) and the headroom matrix (headroom_matrix_v1.xlsx). Please review and respond with final signoff by EOD Thu Aug 27 so I can communicate to Skyline.

If we get signoff, Kimberly: please create the reservation ticket and add Ajay (SRE) for on-call handoff. Marcus: please confirm the MOU or credit path and whether we need a PO.

Attachments: pilot_runbook_draft_v2.pdf, headroom_matrix_v1.xlsx
